transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?
I keep seeing that explosion in my head like it’s happening all over again, and I can’t shut it off. My doctor suggested I come talk to someone because it's just getting to be too much to handle.
How long have these memories of the explosion been coming back like this? Did they start within the past month, or have they been going on for more than a month?

They've been going on for way longer than a month, pretty much ever since the explosion happened about 14 months ago. Instead of fading away over time, it's like they've just dug in and become a constant part of my everyday life.

Since the explosion, have you been going out of your way to avoid reminders of it, like certain places, conversations, or activities? Do you also find yourself trying to push away thoughts or feelings about what happened?

Yes, I definitely do. I’ll drive the long way around just so I don’t have to pass older buildings or that side of town where it happened. And if anyone at church brings up the accident or asks about apprentices, I just shut down the conversation or walk off because I can't stand feeling it all come up.

Since the explosion, have you started feeling persistently guilty, numb, detached from other people, or like you’ve lost interest in things you used to care about? Have you also found yourself blaming yourself or feeling like the world is no longer safe?

I feel completely numb inside, and even when my little niece runs up to hug me, I just can't feel any real happiness anymore. I’ve lost all interest in playing basketball or helping with the church youth program, and I mostly just sit on the couch staring at the TV. I also carry this heavy guilt every single day, hating myself because I survived that blast while my young apprentice didn't.

Since the explosion, have you been feeling constantly on guard or easily startled, and have you had problems with sleep, irritability, or concentrating? These can help me understand how much your body is still reacting to what happened.

I'm constantly on edge and jump out of my skin if someone drops a tool or slams a car door, and it takes forever to stop shaking. Sleep is almost impossible too; I lie awake until two or three in the morning, and if I do doze off, I just jerk awake from fire dreams and end up pacing the room wired.
